hypothesis.statement: Removing the 'Apply deterministic source repairs' step (mobile-source-sync, openapi-generation, dependency-deduplication, eslint-autofix, go-mod-tidy loop, gofmt) from remediation-analysis.yml, renaming it to BThwani Manual Patch Verification, and updating every guard/test/registry/doc marker that names the old workflow text will close GAP-0002 without breaking any of the three consuming guards.

intendedChanges: Remove the whole 'Apply deterministic source repairs' step from remediation-analysis.yml.
Rename the workflow to 'BThwani Manual Patch Verification' and its job to 'Verify candidate source without auto-repair'.
Rename repair-status.tsv to cleanup-status.tsv since only the policy-governed records cleanup remains.
Update required-command-integrity-gate.mjs and check-ci-source-immutability.mjs marker checks to match the new name/job title.
Remove the now-unneeded SOURCE_FORMAT_WRITE remediation exception in check-ci-source-immutability.mjs since no source-rewriting formatter remains in the workflow.
Update check-ci-source-immutability.test.mjs's validRemediation fixture to match.
Update workflow-registry.json's remediation-analysis entry name and purpose, and docs/ci-governance-required-checks.md's PRIVILEGED description.

Review governance/cleanup/repository-retention-policy.json and governance/github/remediation-branch-return-policy.json for required changes; both reference the workflow only by file path, not by name/marker text, so neither needed edits.
forbiddenChanges: Touching any CORE workflow (ci.yml, ci-*.yml, dsh-database.yml, jrn-020-025-sambassam-verify.yml, lockfile-snapshot.yml).
Adding contents:write or any privileged permission.
Adding a repository secret reference to remediation-analysis.yml.

unexpectedResults: governance/cleanup/repository-retention-policy.json and governance/github/remediation-branch-return-policy.json were listed as target files in the original GAP-0002 ledger entry but, on inspection, reference remediation-analysis.yml only by file path (never by name string or step marker), so no edit was required in either; recorded here rather than force-editing them to match a stale nine-file assumption.

guard:workflow-security (zizmor) could not run in this local sandbox because Python is unavailable (Microsoft Store execution-alias stub); this is a pre-existing local-environment limitation unrelated to this change, not a regression it introduced. guard:workflow-lint (actionlint) and guard:actions-pin, which do not depend on Python, both passed against the modernized workflow.

newFindings: The three consuming guards (required-command-integrity-gate.mjs, guard-registry-gate.mjs, check-ci-source-immutability.mjs) key off two different identifiers for remediation-analysis.yml: guard-registry-gate.mjs matches purely by file path, so it needed no edit; the other two match by literal name/step-title strings inside the file content, so both needed synchronized marker updates.

blindSpotsFound: guard:workflow-security (zizmor) has a hard Python-availability dependency that is not satisfiable in this local Windows sandbox; CI itself installs Python so this is not a gap in enforcement, only a local verification blind spot worth noting for future sessions on this machine.
